answer: The strongest lever is simple: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because timber only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, raven is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
